AI for Data Analysis

Chat with a spreadsheet: the model writes code, a sandbox calculates, you check

How ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Copilot analyse files, where they go wrong and how to get an answer you can trust. Case study: Northstar online shop sales, January–June 2026.

← → navigate • N speaker notes • G all slides • F fullscreen
Experiment • 13 Oct 2026

The model did the maths without code — and got it right. Why is that not enough?

Question
Here are sales for January–June (73 CSV rows pasted into the message). What is total revenue? Any data problems?
Claude Haiku 5.5 • no tools
Total revenue is 256,045 (duplicate row 1028 excluded)…
Order 1055: 66 returns on 62 orders — probably a typo, should be 6.
I checked the work: the totals match.
✓
The total is right
On 73 rows modern models do mental maths well. Sonnet 5.5 gave the same total.
✗
“Probably 6” — the source said 4
A guess sounds like a fact. Data must not be fixed by guessing.
✗
“I checked” — with what?
Not a single code run. You cannot see the working or repeat it.
!
100,000 rows will not fit in a message
Real tables mean a file + code, not text in a chat.

How it works

The model is not the calculator. The sandbox is

The model decides what to calculate and writes the code.
The sandbox runs the code and calculates exactly.
You look at the code and check the conclusion.

Step 2 • cleaning

Finding a problem ≠ permission to fix it

Mechanics — OK to fixthe meaning does not change; every change goes into the cleaning log
1028 ×2+$3,312 to revenue
→
keep one rowlog it
region: (empty)row 1010
→
region: UNKNOWNdo not drop the row
2026/04/22row 1041
→
2026-04-22format fixed, but the source has a different day (2026-04-13) → log it
Meaning — do not fixonly the source knows the right value
returns 66on 62 orders, row 1055
→
keep + flagask the data owner
✗
Models guessed: “6”, “6 or 2”
✓
The source had 4
Cleaning log: what changed · which rows · why · how it moved the total. Without a log, cleaning is a silent edit of the data.
GenAI Basics • Lesson 08 • AI for Data Analysis07 / 18
Step 3 • prompt

An analyst’s prompt: question, rules, evidence

Question: how did revenue change from January to June, and which channel grew fastest?
First describe the data: what one row is, how many rows and unique order_ids, gaps, odd values.
Mechanical fixes — do them and log them. If a fix changes the meaning — don’t, ask me.
Calculate revenue by month and by channel, show the code.
Reconcile: sum by month = sum by channel = grand total.
Return: a table, one chart, the cleaning log and one thing this data does not prove.
1question
2profile first
3cleaning rules
4calculation with code
5reconciliation
6what to return

Charts

The question picks the chart type, not looks

How did it change over time?
line
month order matters
Who is bigger?
bars
sort; axis from zero
How are values spread?
histogram
shows outliers
Are two numbers related?
scatter
related ≠ cause
What makes up the whole?
100% bars
no more than 4–5 parts
Ask like this: “Build one chart that answers …, label the axes and units.” Not “make a nice dashboard”.

Step 4 • checking

Check the numbers, not the wording

  1. Rows: 73 before, 1 duplicate removed, 72 left
  2. Totals match three ways (diagram on the left)
  3. Spot check: find row 1063 by eye — Search, June, $5,425
  4. Base of a %: from which number and over which period
  5. Chart = table: points on the chart match the numbers
Rereading the model’s answer is not a check. A check means getting the same number another way.
GenAI Basics • Lesson 08 • AI for Data Analysis13 / 18
Step 5 • the limit of a claim

“What happened” ≠ “what will happen if…”

The trap question from the demo: move budget from Social to Search?
Search$ revenue per $1 of ads
5.52
Social$ revenue per $1 of ads
3.84
Email and Organic: no ad spend — return on ads is not computed.
Honest answer: the data describes the past. To learn the effect — a test: shift part of the budget in one region for 2–4 weeks and compare.

For reference • pandas

What the model writes under the hood

pandas is a Python library for working with tables. Almost every AI analyser uses it.
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("northstar_sales_messy.csv")

print(len(df), df["order_id"].nunique())   # 73 72
print(df[df["returns"] > df["orders"]])  # row 1055

df = df.drop_duplicates("order_id")
df["region"] = df["region"].fillna("UNKNOWN")
df["date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["date"].str.replace("/", "-"))

month = df["date"].dt.to_period("M")
monthly = df.groupby(month)["revenue"].sum()
by_channel = df.groupby("channel")["revenue"].sum()
assert monthly.sum() == by_channel.sum()   # reconcile
This is roughly what you see when you open the code in ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. No need to learn the syntax.
Read what each line means: what was removed, what filled the gap, what it grouped by.
Code verified on our file: total $256,045.

Data and privacy

What you may upload to a chat

OK: practice, public, anonymised data
like our Northstar; any service
Careful: internal company data
only the company work account (ChatGPT Business/Enterprise, Claude Team/Enterprise, Google Workspace) — data is not used for training there
Not without approval: customers, staff, finance, health
personal data — only in an approved environment and with the data owner’s consent
In personal accounts, training on your data depends on settings: ChatGPT — “Improve the model for everyone”, Gemini — “Keep Activity”, Claude — only if you allowed it.
Before uploading: remove unneeded columns (names, phones, e-mails). Sales analysis does not need them.
